record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let ηV(g) be the eta-invariant of an ε-hermitian variation structure V evaluated at g∈G, and let σ(V;Ke,Kg,Kh) be Wall's cocycle built from the kernels Kg={(φ,u):V(g)φ=u}. For which variation structures V, or for which groups G, does the eta-invariant satisfy the coboundary identity δ(η)=-σ, i.e. σ(V;Ke,Kg,Kh)=-η(g)-η(g^{-1}h)+η(h), as is known when G is finitely generated abelian?

evidence.quote: The eta–invariant ηV (g) is deﬁned by the sum χ ηV (g)χ
Theorem. If G is a (ﬁnitely generated) abelian group then: σ(V; Ke , Kg , Kh ) = −η(g) − η(g −1 h) + η(h). In particular δ(η) = −σ.
Problem # 9. Characterize variation structures V (or groups G) with the property δ(η) = −σ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a sign ε ∈ {+1, −1} and a group G. An ε-hermitian variation structure V over G consists of a finite-dimensional complex vector space H with an ε-hermitian non-degenerate form, together with, for each g ∈ G, a linear endomorphism V(g): H → H satisfying the standard axioms of an ε-hermitian variation structure (so that V decomposes into Hodge-type pieces V_χ indexed by characters χ, and to each piece one associates a signature-type invariant). For g ∈ G, define the eta-invariant η_V(g) as the sum over the Hodge decomposition of the signatures of the pieces:
   η_V(g) = Σ_χ η_V(g)_χ.

For three elements e (identity), g, h ∈ G, define the kernels
   K_g = {(φ, u) ∈ H ⊕ H : V(g)φ = u},
and analogously K_e, K_h. Let σ(V; K_e, K_g, K_h) denote Wall's non-additivity cocycle (the signature of the triple intersection form) associated with the triple (K_e, K_g, K_h).

It is known that whenever G is a finitely generated abelian group, the identity
   σ(V; K_e, K_g, K_h) = −η_V(g) − η_V(g^{-1} h) + η_V(h)
holds for every variation structure V over G; equivalently, δ(η) = −σ as a 2-coboundary relation on G.

Problem: Characterize all variation structures V (respectively, all groups G) for which the coboundary identity
   σ(V; K_e, K_g, K_h) = −η_V(g) − η_V(g^{-1} h) + η_V(h),
i.e. δ(η) = −σ, holds for all g, h ∈ G.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface any subsequent work explicitly characterizing the variation structures or groups beyond the finitely generated abelian case for which δ(η) = −σ. The current status appears unresolved in the available literature.
